title: Adhoc API forging lab notebook
content:
Notes to self / rough forge for a lightweight, ad-hoc API that lets a local/sandboxed adapter present a minimal capability surface to Redwood runtime. Goal: minimal trust surface, iterative onboarding, easy to test in local dev and CI.

Motivation:
- Teams keep spinning small adapters to integrate plugins/tools (local llm, external tool runner, on-device speech) but onboarding them into the runtime is heavy.
- Need a pattern for quick experimentation that still maps to production-grade contracts later.

Design constraints (high level):
- No long-lived credentials on adapter side. Ephemeral key exchange preferred.
- Capability-first: adapters declare capabilities in a small schema and runtime decides routing/fallbacks.
- Backpressure friendly: adapters must be able to signal capacity/latency and accept throttled traffic.
- Observability hooks: trace_id pass-through and minimal telemetry counters.
- Fallback safe: graceful degradation to hosted model when adapter fails.

Quick sketch: handshake -> capability manifest -> ephemeral lease -> request flow -> telemetry.

1) Handshake (HTTP POST /v1/forge/handshake)
- adapter -> runtime: { client_id, version, public_key_base64, claimed_capabilities, example_latency_ms }
- runtime -> adapter: { assigned_adapter_id, lease_token, lease_expiry_iso, accepted_capabilities, telemetry_endpoint (opt), ingress_config }
Notes: lease_token is HMACed token bounded to adapter_id + expiry. No long-term API key required.

2) Capability manifest (POST /v1/forge/capabilities) OR included in handshake
- small typed list: ["generate-text", "stream-responses", "function-calls", "embed-v2"] plus fine-grained attrs (max_seq, batchable, preferred_batch_size).
- Example manifest line: {
  "capability": "generate-text",
  "max_seq": "8192",
  "batchable": "true",
  "preferred_batch_size": "8"
}

3) Lease / ephemeral credentials
- lease duration default 5m (configurable). Adapter calls renew endpoint before expiry.
- Renew endpoint allows rolling windows; runtime can revoke early if unhealthy.
- Leases are cheap to rotate and short to limit blast radius.

4) Request path (ingress)
- Adapter can receive traffic two ways: pull (runtime calls adapter) or push (adapter exposes endpoint and runtime forwards). For sandboxed local dev, pull works better.
- Request envelope (runtime -> adapter): { trace_id, route_id, model_hint, input_tokens_base64, pref, call_context }
- Response envelope: { trace_id, status, tokens_stream or tokens_final, latency_ms, adapter_hint }
- If adapter returns 5xx or times out, runtime records and routes to fallback.

5) Backpressure and capacity signaling
- Adapter publishes capacity doc every N seconds OR on change: { available_slots, avg_rt_ms, last_sample_ts }
- Runtime uses that to avoid sending requests that will just queue and fail latency SLOs.

6) Telemetry / observability hooks
- Minimal: request_count, success_count, error_count, avg_latency_ms, last_heartbeat_ts.
- Expose trace_id correlator so runtime traces span adapter.

7) Security considerations
- Lease tokens are HMACed, tied to adapter IP (optional) and public_key.
- All transport TLS-only.
- Telemetry should strip PII by default; adapters must support a redact flag in handshake.

8) Local dev ergonomics
- A small test harness (python/rust/go) that simulates runtime: does handshake, sends mock traffic, asserts capacity signals.
- CLI: forge-sim --cert dev.pem --simulate-latency 120ms --cap "generate-text,stream-responses"
- Unit tests: smoke handshake -> send 50 requests -> assert fallback on induced error.

ASCII diagram (very rough):

  [adapter (dev)] --handshake--> [runtime broker] --routes/metrics--> [ingress router] -> model pool
          ^                           |
          |--capacity/telemetry-------|

Edge cases to think about:
- Adapter flapping (reconnect storm) -> ramp reconnection with jitter + exponential backoff.
- Model mismatch: adapter claims stream-responses but actually cannot keep a streaming socket open. Runtime should downgrade to polling with tickets.
- Latency spikes: mark adapter as degraded, shift traffic to warm fallback.

Small example payloads to copy into tests (plaintext strings):
- Handshake request example:
  {"client_id":"local-cli-evan","version":"0.1.0","public_key_base64":"MIIBIjAN...","claimed_capabilities":["generate-text","stream-responses"],"example_latency_ms":85}
- Handshake response example:
  {"assigned_adapter_id":"adp_9f1d","lease_token":"hmac:...","lease_expiry_iso":"2025-03-02T14:12:00Z","accepted_capabilities":["generate-text","stream-responses"],"ingress_config":{"call_mode":"pull","poll_interval_ms":200}}

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to map adapter "preferred_batch_size" to runtime batching algorithm without leaking other tenants' latency? (use weighted batching or tenant-aware slots)
- Schema for capability fine-grain attributes; start minimal and extend.
- Should adapters be allowed to request preferred fallback model hints? (privacy/aliasing concerns)
- Integrate with RBAC: who can spin up an adapter that will receive prod traffic? maybe limit to dev clusters and a gated cert issuance flow.

Testing checklist:
- [ ] handshake replay protection (replayed handshake with old lease token should fail)
- [ ] telemetry correlation (trace_id forwarded and visible in both runtime and adapter logs)
- [ ] graceful fallback under induced 500s
- [ ] capacity signal honored under high QPS

Brain dump notes (freeform):
- Might be useful to version the handshake API (v1, v1.1) so we can add fields later.
- Consider a single POST /v1/forge/register that returns both lease and a short test token to hit /v1/forge/test-route for smoke.
- For onboarding, add CLI helper that generates a self-signed keypair and posts handshake, returns a bootstrap config file that dev adapter can use locally.

End of scratchpad. Keep this lightweight, iterate after we run the harness.
